prerequisites: Basic knowledge of probability theory and statistics (cfr. Probability Theory and Statistics H01A6A).

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with insight into how uncertain factors are taken into account in the design, construction and maintenance of structures and how the calculation methods used for this are performed.
Calculate failure probabilities using the FOSM and FORM method.
Perform a system reliability analysis using FORM results for the components.
Explain in depth why and how partial safety factors are derived in design codes.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the principles of safe design: nomenclature, acceptability criteria, levels of reliability analysis, partial safety factors, return periods, characteristic values, code calibration
First-Order Second-Moment (FOSM) reliability calculation and Hasofer-Lind reliability index
Implementation with EXCEL of the FORM method and application to simple didactic problems (in PC-classes). A report of the solutions must be submitted with the exam.
Guided solution of example exam questions.

assessment_methods.method: Evaluation of the report of the solutions to the exercises
Solution of open questions posed during the exam

assessment_rules: The final mark is composed of 25% from the report of the exercise solutions and 75% from the written exam. For the resit, the report of the exercises no longer counts; the evaluation is then 100% based on the exam.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
